Container.Name: DOOM
Container.Overview:
The original 1997 linuxdoom-1.10 sources, built from source and playable in a browser.
The container runs its own X server (Xvfb) and exports it over noVNC, so nothing needs to be installed on the host.
Sound comes out of the browser, with nothing to set up. Effects and music - the music converted from the WAD's MUS lumps to MIDI and rendered by FluidSynth - are mixed inside the container and sent to the same page as the picture, over the WebUI port you already mapped. Click to start playing and the sound starts with it, because browsers will not play audio without a click.
The shareware game data is included, so this plays as soon as it starts - episode 1, nine levels. To play the full game, put your own DOOM.WAD, DOOM2.WAD, TNT.WAD or PLUTONIA.WAD into the WADs folder below and it will be used instead. The name is matched without regard to case. Commercial game data is not included and must come from your own copy of the game.
The WebUI opens a client that captures the mouse, so turning does not run out of screen and the cursor stays in the game. Escape hands the cursor back, and the ` key opens the game menu whatever the mouse is doing. Plain noVNC is still there at /vnc.html if you would rather it did not grab the pointer, though it carries no sound.
A game controller works too, on a phone as well as a desktop - an Xbox pad, a Backbone One, anything the browser reports as a standard gamepad - and it vibrates when you fire or are hurt, where the browser can drive the pad's motors. It is set up in the game, under Options - Setup - Controller. On a phone the controller is the whole of the input, and the sound comes out of the phone's own speaker.
Keys, the mouse and the controller are set from inside the game, under Options - Setup. The same menu lists the WAD files in the folder below and loads the one you pick, so mods can be dropped in and switched to without touching the container settings.
Container.Requires: Nothing. The shareware game data ships with the container. Add your own IWAD to the WADs folder to play the full game.
Container.Changes:
### 1.10.70 - 1.10.73 - Fixes a crash that could end the game at a level change. The music is rendered on a thread of its own while the game replaces the player on every new level, and nothing was keeping the two apart - so the renderer could be reading something that had just been freed. Rare, unpredictable, and it looked like a fault in the music library rather than in this. - A crash, or choosing QUIT GAME, now starts the game again instead of taking the container down with it. The picture, the sound and the session all stay up, so the browser reconnects on its own. Set DOOM_RESTART=0 for the old behaviour. - On a phone the sound now comes out of the phone's own speaker rather than a plugged-in controller's headphone socket.
### 1.10.63 - 1.10.69 - Fixes for game controllers, most of which were not the controller's fault: a saved layout hid every button added to the game after it was saved, the start screen never went away on an iPhone so the pad was never allowed to send anything, and a control bound to Enter could never work because the game takes that key for itself before the level ever sees it. - The container's log now says what the controller is doing - which pad was found, what each control will send, and what it actually sent - so "the controller does not work" can be answered from docker logs. - A crash now prints where it died instead of the single word "Segmentation fault".
### 1.10.51 - 1.10.62 - A game controller works, on a phone as well as a desktop. Every button is rebindable from the start screen, the sticks have a deadzone, turn speed and invert, and the layout is saved per browser. - The controller presses the keys this engine is actually bound to, read from its own config, so rebinding in Options - Setup - Controls does not leave the pad pressing the old ones. - The start screen is quiet unless something is wrong. Add ?stats=1 to the address for the sound and picture measurements.
### 1.10.48 - 1.10.50 - Quitting the game no longer reports a fault on the way out. - The stutter fixed in 1.10.47 is written up in full in DOCKER.md, with the measurements.
### 1.10.47 - Fixes the stutter: the picture pausing for about a third of a second, usually while you were shooting. x11vnc was watching for a window being dragged whenever a mouse button was held down, and holding the picture back while it decided - which in a game is all the time. With the fire button held that is now 554 KB/s at a 12 ms median instead of 257 KB/s at 41 ms. Nothing to change; pull and play.
### 1.10.46 - The container now says when one of its own pieces dies, and stops, instead of sitting there looking healthy while the browser says "connection lost". - An x11vnc option typed without its leading dash is refused at startup with the correction named, rather than killing the picture a second later.
### 1.10.39 - 1.10.45 - Tools for finding the stutter above, none of which change how it plays: doom-probe, which times how long x11vnc takes to answer and can tell a real stall from a screen that simply was not changing, and a picture readout on the start screen. See DOCKER.md if you ever need them.
### 1.10.30 - Fixes the sound being left permanently out of step if the browser's socket filled up, which could leave it crackling until you reloaded.
### 1.10.29 - The engine no longer waits for the X server to confirm each frame, which was costing 74 ms a frame under load.
### 1.10.28 - Escape reliably releases the mouse and brings the start screen back, in both fullscreen and windowed, instead of depending on what the browser does with it.
### 1.10.25 - The engine was spinning on a core while waiting for the next frame, starving everything else in the container. It sleeps properly now: 96% of a core down to 5%.
### 1.10.24 - Fixes the pause when something new appears - a door opening, a monster waking. The engine was re-reading the game data from the WAD during play instead of keeping it, 230 times in three minutes.
### 1.10.23 - Sound effects are mixed where they are sent, and the separate 1997 sound server is gone from the browser path. The sound now arrives 14 ms behind the picture instead of 102 ms.
### 1.10.22 - Corrects 1.10.21's note: the delay between a keypress and seeing it is about 48 ms, not 140. The 140 ms figure was mostly the pistol's own wind-up animation, which the game has always had. - Fixes the sound getting later the longer you play, sound never working anywhere but localhost, and a buffer that could underrun for ever without growing.
### 1.10.21 - Small VNC timing changes, and notes on why the picture lags about 140 ms behind the keypress - it is the VNC round trip, and none of the usual settings affect it. The sound is unchanged and still arrives promptly. (The 140 ms was wrong; see 1.10.22 above. It is about 48 ms, and most of that is the engine's own frame rate.)
### 1.10.20 - Fixes the sound getting later the longer you play. It drifted because the container and your sound card keep slightly different time and nothing corrected for it; now the playback rate is nudged imperceptibly to hold the delay steady.
### 1.10.19 - The sound arrives about 220 ms sooner. Most of what remains is the picture itself, which takes about the same time to come back over VNC.
### 1.10.18 - Fixes sound not working at all. It was played through a browser feature only offered over HTTPS or localhost, which a container reached at http://your-server:6080 is neither - so it failed everywhere except the one arrangement it was tested in. There is now a fallback that needs neither.
### 1.10.17 - The start screen now shows what the sound is doing and which build the page came from, and the container prints its own build at startup. If there is no sound, those three things say why between them.
### 1.10.16 - Fixes 1.10.15's sound not arriving in some browsers: the page was being served from the browser cache, from before the sound existed. No more hard reloads after an update. - When there is no sound, the page now says why instead of staying quiet.
### 1.10.15 - Sound comes out of the browser. Effects and music are mixed in the container and sent to the same page as the picture, over the WebUI port you already mapped - nothing to install, nothing to mount. It starts with the click that starts play.
### 1.10.14 - The ` key opens the game menu, in every mode. Escape still does when the browser lets it through, which in a window it does not. - Every menu is drawn at one size, and the added options fit.
### 1.10.13 - You can now play in the window instead of fullscreen; both capture the mouse.
### 1.10.12 - Fixes a crash loop caused by the Graphic Detail option in the game's own Options menu. An affected config repairs itself; nothing to edit.
### 1.10.11 - A rendering glitch no longer ends the game, and the log says what caused it.
### 1.10.10 - A bad screen-size value in the config no longer breaks the renderer or puts the container into a crash loop.
### 1.10.9 - The mouse turns you without also walking you forward and back. Options - Setup - Mouse - MOVE WITH MOUSE restores the original behaviour. - PUID=0 starts instead of looping.
### 1.10.8 - Holding a mouse button repeats the action, and releasing it stops.
### 1.10.7 - Mouse look actually works. Most of the movement was being discarded before it reached the game. - The picture fills the window instead of sitting small in the corner. - The mouse capture no longer fails silently when you click to play.
### 1.10.6 - Mouse look turns properly. Most of the movement was being discarded before it reached the game. - Mouse buttons no longer stick on after the mouse capture is released. - Fullscreen fills the screen, keeping the picture's shape.
### 1.10.5 - Mouse look turns properly instead of jittering in place.
### 1.10.4 - Escape opens the game menu again while the mouse is captured, instead of letting the mouse go. Hold Escape to release it and leave fullscreen. - The menu can be put on a second key of your choosing, under Options - Setup - Controls, for browsers that will not give Escape up.
### 1.10.3 - The Ultimate Doom is recognised properly. Re-releases install it as DOOM.WAD, which the engine read as three-episode Doom, so Thy Flesh Consumed could not be reached. It is identified by its contents now. - With both games in the WADs folder, Doom starts rather than Doom II. Set DOOM_IWAD to choose. - The attract demos play instead of being rejected, and two 1997 bugs that filled the log with repeated warnings are fixed. - The WebUI address now goes straight to the client that captures the mouse.
### 1.10.2 - The shareware game data ships with the container, so it plays as soon as it starts. Your own IWAD still takes precedence when you add one. - The mouse is captured in the browser now, so turning no longer stops partway and the cursor cannot slide out of the window. - The game claims the keyboard focus for itself instead of relying on where the pointer happens to be.
### 1.10.1 - Options - Setup, with three new pages: rebind keys, configure the mouse, and pick a WAD from the mounted folder without restarting the container. - The mouse works. Pointer events never reached the engine before, and the filter for its own re-centring threw away most of the motion that did. - The picture is no longer stretched: the browser client renders 320x200 at the scale you set instead of scaling it to the window. - Fixed a crash on quit that hit roughly one exit in three.
### 1.10.0 - First release. The 1997 linuxdoom-1.10 sources repaired to build and run on 64-bit Linux, with sound effects and music added, played in a browser over noVNC. Game data is not included; supply your own IWAD.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port for the browser client, carrying both the picture and the sound. Open the WebUI to play.

Config.Name: VNC Port
Config.Description: Optional. Only needed if you want to connect with a native VNC client instead of the browser.

Config.Name: WADs
Config.Description: Optional. The shareware game data is already in the container. Put your own DOOM.WAD, DOOM2.WAD, TNT.WAD or PLUTONIA.WAD here to play the full game; it takes precedence over the shareware file. Mounted read only; the container never writes to it.

Config.Name: Saves and config
Config.Description: Savegames, the .doomrc config file and the container's logs.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: UID the game runs as. Must be able to write the saves folder. Unraid default: 99 (nobody).

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: GID the game runs as. Unraid default: 100 (users).

Config.Name: Scale
Config.Description: Pixel scale, 1 to 4. The picture is 320x200 multiplied by this, so 2 gives 640x400. Larger values cost more bandwidth to the browser.

Config.Name: Which IWAD
Config.Description: Optional. With several games in the WADs folder, which one to start - a filename such as doom2.wad. Leave empty and Doom is preferred over Doom II.

Config.Name: Sound
Config.Description: Set to 0 for no sound at all, which saves the bandwidth the audio stream uses.

Config.Name: Restart on crash
Config.Description: Start the game again if it crashes or you choose QUIT GAME, leaving the container up so the browser reconnects on its own. Set to 0 to have the container stop instead.

Config.Name: VNC Password
Config.Description: Optional. If set, the browser and any VNC client must supply this password. Leave empty for no password, which is fine on a LAN you trust.

Config.Name: Audio rate
Config.Description: Rate the sound reaches the browser at, in Hz. 22050 is the default and costs about 700 kbit/s. Use 11025 to halve that, or 44100 to double it.

Config.Name: PulseAudio server
Config.Description: Optional, and not what most people want. Leave empty and the sound goes to the browser. Set this to a reachable PulseAudio server, for example tcp:192.168.1.50:4713, and the sound goes there instead - to speakers attached to that machine, not to yours.

Config.Name: Soundfont
Config.Description: Optional. Path inside the container to a General MIDI soundfont for music. Leave empty to use the one built into the image.
